title: Nitesh Tiwari Confirms Ramayana Part One Ends on a Cliffhanger as Sony Pictures Joins Global Release
excerpt: The director revealed at San Diego Comic-Con that the epic's two-part structure builds to an emotionally charged ending, with the trailer now expected July 29 ahead of a November Diwali release.
body:
• Director Nitesh Tiwari confirmed at San Diego Comic-Con that Ramayana Part One will end on a major cliffhanger designed to make audiences want Part Two "the moment they leave the theatre."
  • Sony Pictures Entertainment has come on board for international distribution, marking the first time a Hollywood studio will handle the global release of a Ramayana adaptation.
  • The trailer, postponed from its planned Comic-Con debut, is now expected to drop online on July 29 and will be attached to Spider-Man: Brand New Day prints from July 30.
  • The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Sunny Deol as Hanuman, with Part One releasing on November 8 and Part Two targeting Diwali 2027.

A Cliffhanger by Design

Nitesh Tiwari has answered the question that has been hanging over India's most anticipated film: where does Part One end?

https://youtube.com/watch?v=g0YoWyhNKfM

Speaking at San Diego Comic-Con during a panel for Ramayana, the director confirmed that the first instalment will conclude on a major cliffhanger — a narrative choice designed to leave audiences demanding the sequel.

"Ramayana is a linear story, and where we leave off in Part One is something you can call a cliffhanger," Tiwari told IGN. "Something that will make people want to watch Part Two the moment they leave the theatre. It's a story that deserves two parts. It cannot be told in one part, and we just decided that this would probably be the best juncture to leave it on in Part One, leaving the rest for Part Two."

While Tiwari noted that Indian audiences familiar with the epic might anticipate the break point, he suggested the cliffhanger would generate massive excitement among international viewers encountering the story for the first time on this scale.

Sony Pictures and Global Ambitions

The Comic-Con appearance underscored just how big the ambitions are for this project. Prime Focus Studios announced a landmark partnership with Sony Pictures Entertainment for international distribution — making Ramayana the first big-screen adaptation of the Hindu epic to be distributed globally by a Hollywood studio.

https://x.com/MissMalini/status/2081643790427996376

Producer Namit Malhotra called the deal a "historic moment." The partnership means the trailer will be attached to Spider-Man: Brand New Day prints in cinemas from July 30, giving Ramayana exposure alongside one of 2026's biggest Hollywood releases. The trailer itself, postponed from its planned Comic-Con debut due to "unforeseen circumstances," is now expected to drop online on July 29.

The film has also been officially designated as "Filmed For IMAX" — shot with IMAX-certified cameras for an expanded aspect ratio, positioning it alongside global Hollywood spectacles like Dune and Avengers in the premium format space.

"The same story, which many people may have heard and seen before, will be absolutely refreshing. This is an absolutely fresh take on that in terms of execution."

— Nitesh Tiwari, Director

The Cast and the Scale

The ensemble cast has been a talking point since the project was first announced. Ranbir Kapoor steps into the role of Lord Ram — a performance that reportedly required months of physical transformation and yoga training. Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash takes on Ravana, and Sunny Deol rounds out the principal cast as Hanuman, with Ravi Dubey also in a key role.

At Comic-Con, Yash defended Kapoor's casting against criticism that has followed the announcement. "He is a fabulous actor," Yash said, while Kapoor himself spoke candidly about the pressure. "There was so much fear, so much doubt," the actor said of preparing for the role.

What's Next

Ramayana: Part One is scheduled for release on November 8, ahead of Diwali. Part Two is planned for Diwali 2027. Dharma Productions has secured the Indian distribution rights. For the Indian diaspora worldwide, the Sony partnership means the film will have the widest global theatrical footprint of any Indian mythological epic — a far cry from the limited international runs that even major Bollywood releases typically manage.
